The user wants the map 20x bigger, and buildings 10x bigger. Currently WORLD = 448, VIEW_SIZE = 160, MAP_SCALE = WORLD/160 = 2.8.

Let me understand the coordinate model. Entities positions x,y are in [0,1] normalized. World coordinates: (x-.5)*WORLD. Camera view: ortho width = VIEW_SIZE * aspect / zoom. So at zoom 1, view spans 160 world units. The map is 448 wide. So the map is 2.8 screens wide at zoom 1.

"Map is still too small. Increase it another 20 times bigger." So WORLD should go from 448 to 8960. But then the normalized positions still map across the whole map, so everything (units distances etc.) need to be rescaled to keep the game playable. Hmm.

Actually if we just increase WORLD to 20x and keep positions normalized, then the map is 20x larger physically but the layout is identical — the same fraction of the map is used. Distances between things (measured in screen px) would grow 20x, so units would take forever to cross, and weapons ranges stay the same (in screen px, because range measured via toScreen with MAP_SCALE).

Wait: distance() uses toScreen with viewScale = camera.z*MAP_SCALE where MAP_SCALE=WORLD/160. So world-normalized distance converted to screen pixels with MAP_SCALE. If WORLD increases 20x, MAP_SCALE increases 20x, and distances in screen px increase 20x at same camera.z. But viewScale also used to convert world to screen -> at camera.z=1 the whole 160 world units visible... hmm wait toScreen: (x-camera.x)*scale+.5 where scale=viewScale. So screen normalized coordinate = normalized world delta * MAP_SCALE * zoom. Since normalized world delta = world delta/WORLD, screen fraction = world delta/160 * zoom. That's consistent: at zoom 1, 160 world units fill the view.

So increasing WORLD alone means the normalized positions spread over 20x more world units, so everything appears 20x farther apart in world units, and on screen at zoom 1 20x farther apart. So indeed "map is 20x bigger" but everything else stays same fraction — so at any given zoom, units appear the same relative position but the actual world scale makes units look tiny relative to the terrain? No — units scale in renderer is set via `entity.size/70`, independent of WORLD. Building model is ~14 units wide and scale = size/70 where size=45 -> 0.64, so actual footprint ~9 units. World is 448. So buildings are ~2% of map width. If WORLD goes 20x, buildings become 0.1% of map width — invisible specks. That's why the user says buildings are tiny and wants 10x.

Hmm, but the request: "Map is still too small. Increase it another 20 times bigger. The buildings are also tiny. Increase their size by 10 times." So we need to scale buildings 10x in world units, and map 20x. But then what about units, ranges, speeds? If everything stays in normalized [0,1] coords and WORLD grows, unit speed is defined in normalized units per sec? Let's check movement: dx=(dest.x-u.x)*width (screen px), step = speed*dt (px), then u.x += dx/d*step/width. So movement is in screen pixels per second at current zoom. speed=44 px/s. So units move at constant screen pixels per second regardless of zoom, which means speed depends on WORLD: in world units, speed = 44/WORLD*160... i.e., normalized speed = 44/(width*viewScale) — wait, step/width in normalized; viewScale depends on WORLD. So world-unit speed = step/viewScale. With WORLD 20x, viewScale 20x, world speed decreases 20x. So on screen everything looks the same relative to camera at same zoom! The normalized layout is identical.

So essentially if we just increase WORLD 20x, the game looks identical at zoom=1 because positions normalized and all distances scale together. The map *feels* bigger only if we zoom in and pan. But the actual fraction of distance traversal relative to viewport stays the same. Hmm.

Actually, wait. There are two "world" scales: normalized [0,1] used for logic, and renderer WORLD. Increasing WORLD while keeping all in normalized coords means nothing visually changes except: building render scale (size/70) doesn't depend on WORLD so buildings become 20x smaller relative to map/world. Also weapons ranges measured via distance() in screen px and viewScale, which is proportional; ranges are fixed screen px so relative to viewport stays. So actually increasing WORLD alone doesn't change gameplay except buildings shrink. Hmm, MAP_SCALE changes, but distances in screen px: distance uses (p.x-q.x)*width where p.x delta = (a.x-b.x)*viewScale; viewScale = camera.z*WORLD/160. So screen px distance = deltaNorm * camera.z*WORLD/160 * width. Ranges are in screen px, so with WORLD 20x, deltaNorm effective range becomes 1/20. So ranges cover 1/20 of normalized map! So units would need to be 20x closer to engage. That's a real gameplay change: everything gets much smaller relative.

Hmm, so the current architecture ties "screen px" units to gameplay while also tying map physical size. The user's perception: "Map is still too small" - they likely zoomed out and could see the whole map, and buildings tiny. This suggests previous iteration already scaled. Then make buildings 10x bigger in renderer (scale factor size/70*10?). And scale all gameplay ranges/speeds distances to world units so the game remains playable, and also spread entities/base across the bigger map so there's actually a big map to traverse.

But caution: if we keep normalized positions and increase WORLD 20x and scale building render 10x and scale ranges 20x (so relative to normalized map same as before), then the map looks/plays identical to before but buildings are 10x bigger. ## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Increase the battlefield scale and building sizes in the existing RTS game so the map feels noticeably larger and structures are more prominent.

## Requirements
- Map is still too small; increase it another 20x larger.
- Buildings are too small; increase their size by 10x.
- Keep the game complete, playable, and reasonably balanced.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when complete.

## Decisions
- Expanded the world and camera framing to support a much larger battlefield while preserving playability.
- Kept enemy bases spaced away from the player base and added a buildup phase before hostile pressure ramps up.
- Kept the existing RTS structure and faction system, adjusting scale rather than rewriting the game.

## Work State
Break the objective into smaller goals and report which are completed, which are being worked on, and which are blocked.
### Completed
- Expanded the gameplay map and renderer world scale for a much larger theater.
- Increased the effective presence of buildings and combat units through larger scene scaling and model proportions.
- Added a wider enemy buildup window before the assault begins to preserve pacing.
- Kept the game playable in the current build with enemy and player base logic intact.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Verify the battlefield and building scale in a browser, then tune if the map still feels undersized or the structures still read too small.
2. If needed, apply a final pass to camera framing and unit/building proportions based on the actual render.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: main gameplay logic, world scale, build setup, map pacing, and enemy progression.
- `renderer3d.js`: 3D world size, camera framing, terrain generation, and model scaling/visual mass.
- `index.html`: UI shell and game entry point.
- `screenshots/`: screenshot output location for visual verification when needed.

## Important Context
- The latest request was a follow-up change to an already-expanded map/building scale, not a brand-new project.
- The work already applied in code adjusted map scale and base timing with the intent of making the battlefield feel much more open and the structures more imposing.
